Consider direct sowing rather than transplanting as this can lead to reduced pressure by pests.
Monitoring: Monitor crops regularly, notably on a weekly basis during early growth.
Common symptoms include white or transparent patches and yellowish blocthing with pin holes on leaves and stem.
Other symptoms include drooping of young leaves, shrivelled plant, stunted growth, fragile stems and yellow spots on inner leaf margin.
Consider direct control actions when 1-2 eggs per hill are found and chemical control when 15-30% leaf damage is observed.
